chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

"No servant is there but he is awakened once or twice or multiple times in every night. If he rises [for prayer], that is [good]; but if not, the Shaytan urinates in his ear. And does not one of you see that when he rises and it was not his [habitual] action, he rises heavy and sluggish?"
ai.seo_question: What happens spiritually if a person does not rise for night prayer?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the universal spiritual struggle against *ghawwa* (spiritual heaviness), noting that even the righteous are awakened to combat the Shaytan's influence. The imagery of the Shaytan urinating in the ear signifies the degradation of the soul that remains passive, while the physical sluggishness described reflects the natural resistance of the *nafs* to voluntary worship. This underscores the Shia emphasis on *Munajat* and *Tahajjud* as essential disciplines to purify the heart and overcome the inertia of the self.
